# AI Inference Gateway

The AI Inference Gateway governs agent access to large language models (LLMs) in
Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric. It provides a supported inference interface between
applications and model providers, with policy controls for routing, usage, and
sensitive data.

@include '../../../global/partials/alerts/beta.mdx'

Agents reach the gateway over their Consul service mesh path. The gateway
forwards each request to a model registered in the Consul catalog. To learn how
model, tool, and identity paths fit together, refer to the [Consul Agentic
Runtime Fabric architecture](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/architecture).

@include 'alerts/enterprise-alert.mdx'

## Introduction

Applications send inference requests to a gateway instead of integrating network policy separately for each provider. The gateway accepts an OpenAI-compatible request format and translates supported operations to the selected provider's format. Interface compatibility does not imply support for every provider feature or equivalent behavior between models.

Consul supplies gateway configuration and eligible backend information. Envoy enforces mesh connectivity policy and performs routing and retries. The external processor validates and transforms requests and responses. It does not independently select routes or run a retry loop.

## Deployment prerequisites

To install and enable the AI Inference Gateway, refer to [Install Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/install). To register models and deploy a gateway, refer to [Configure the AI Inference Gateway](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/inference-gateway/configure).

## Request processing

The inference path separates processing before and after Envoy selects an upstream:

| Phase | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Before routing | Resolve caller workload identity, validate the canonical request, and apply configured request-side data protection. Provide request information used by configured routing policy. |
| After routing | Translate the request for the selected provider and rewrite the provider request path. |
| Provider response | Normalize supported responses, process streamed output where supported, apply configured response-side data protection, and capture usage. |

The upstream processor uses information about the backend that Envoy selected. A retry against another backend must use that backend's adapter and model information rather than reuse an incompatible translated request.

## Model routing and failover

The gateway routes each request in one of two modes. The `Processor.BodyModelRouting` field in the [`inference-gateway` configuration entry](/consul/docs/reference/config-entry/inference-gateway) selects the mode.

| Mode | How the gateway routes | When it applies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Capability routing | Routes on a capability that the caller sends in a request header. | Default, when `BodyModelRouting` is `false`. |
| Body model routing | Routes on the model named in the request body. | When `BodyModelRouting` is `true`. |

The Consul catalog decides which models serve a capability and in what order. Each model service declares its capabilities and a priority for each one. Service intentions decide which models the gateway can reach.

When two or more models serve a capability, Envoy fails a request over across their priority tiers. The `Failover` block controls which conditions trigger a retry, how many tiers one request can try, and the timeout for each attempt. `RequestTimeout` sets one deadline for the whole request across every attempt.

Provider translation changes the wire format. It does not establish that two models have the same capabilities, quality, or data-handling terms.

## Data protection and streaming

Personally identifiable information (PII) processing applies the configured detection and handling rules to request or response content. Request-side controls act before data reaches a provider. Response-side controls act before processed content returns to the caller.

Configure detection in the `PII` block of the `inference-gateway` configuration entry:

- **Detectors.** Use the built-in `api_key`, `credit_card`, `email`, and `ssn` detectors, or define a custom detector with an RE2 regular expression. The `credit_card` detector also checks the Luhn digit.
- **Actions.** Each match is replaced with a placeholder, masked, blocked, or ignored. The actions are `placeholder`, `mask`, `block`, and `off`.
- **Scope.** Apply detection to requests, responses, or both. The processor defaults to requests.
- **Streaming.** `StreamHoldbackBytes` sets how much trailing content the gateway withholds from a streamed response, so that it catches a match split across chunks.

Streaming introduces an additional boundary: content already delivered to the caller cannot be recalled. Validate detector coverage, buffering behavior, and supported stream formats for your deployment. Do not interpret configured PII controls as a guarantee that all sensitive content is detected.

Operational metrics and decision logs record bounded metadata, not prompts, responses, detected PII values, credentials, or provider error text that can contain request content. Content-bearing payload traces require separate approval and filtering or redaction under the [auto-instrumentation privacy controls](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/observability/auto-instrumentation#payload-span-sensitive-data-security).

## Automatic instrumentation

The AI Inference Gateway is a specialized proxy that [automatically instruments supported model exchanges](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/observability/auto-instrumentation). Gateway tracing is off by default. Enable it with the `Observability.Tracing` block in the `inference-gateway` configuration entry, as described in [Configure auto-instrumentation](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/observability/configure-auto-instrumentation#enable-inference-gateway-tracing). Its Envoy and protocol-aware external-processing components generate network and AI payload spans without application tracing SDKs or manual spans. Applications preserve trace context across calls; model usage and responses do not establish business-level task completion.

Agentic Analytics can use the correlated evidence for [cycle detection](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/cycle-detection). Detection and agent-scoped enforcement require the analytics, policy, and protection-state path in addition to gateway tracing.

## Dependencies and boundaries

- Mesh identity and policy establish the workload's permitted network path to the gateway and its backends.
- Provider adapters define supported request formats, response formats, streaming behavior, and translation limits.
- The Consul catalog and service intentions define eligible model backends.
- Managed-model authentication is separate from delegated user identity and external credential injection.

The inference component owns adapter behavior, streaming, routing-rule integration, and PII processing. It does not own tool business logic or determine whether a model response satisfies the user's task.
